title: Unified SDK recovery patterns and user-centric error telemetry
creator: Samir Patel
description: Define and implement a cross-language set of recovery helpers and a developer-friendly error surface for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is to provide consistent, actionable error messages, deterministic retry semantics, and ergonomics for resumable streaming while emitting telemetry that enables fast incident diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: A single error-code to high-level-category mapping is defined and documented (network, transient-service, rate-limit, auth, model-degraded, client-usage)
SDKs expose a RetryPolicy object and a lightweight RetryContext that surfaces retryable vs terminal decisions with machine-readable hints
Streaming SDKs (all three languages) provide a StreamCheckpoint abstraction and example pattern to resume short-lived interruptions without duplicating application side-effects
All SDKs attach an opaque stable error_id and correlation_id to errors and surface human-friendly remediation suggestions in the message
Telemetry schema examples and recommended logs/span fields documented and a central table mapping SDK error codes to telemetry 'error_class' values
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff. Discussed current inconsistencies across SDKs: Python uses exception subclassing, TS uses string codes, Go returns typed errors—causes subtle divergence in retry logic.
2026-03-11: Decided core surface: (1) numeric error_code, (2) error_class string, (3) stable error_id (UUID v4), (4) correlation_id (request-based), (5) human_message and machine_hints list.

2026-03-12: Prototyped Python RetryContext and StreamCheckpoint. Early feedback from solutions eng: StreamCheckpoint API must be explicit about idempotency requirements and not encourage anti-patterns that hide side-effects.

2026-03-12: Telemetry: agreed fields for traces/logs: error_class, error_code, error_id, correlation_id, sdk_lang, sdk_version, endpoint, model, latency_ms, retry_attempts. Added note to avoid logging request payloads by default.
2026-03-13: Trade-off decision: do not attempt automatic replay of streamed messages for arbitrary user handlers. Offer a resume token and clear docs + examples for safe resumptions.
Follow-ups: Add a migration guide for TS & Go users that currently rely on string-based error checks; add incubating 'typed' helpers in next minor release.
design_decisions: Expose both machine_hints (enum-like token list) and a short human_message to keep runtime decision logic deterministic while staying user-friendly.
Keep numeric error_code stable across SDKs; map existing HTTP/gRPC statuses into our error_class and error_code ranges to reduce ambiguity.
Streaming resume exposes a small checkpoint token (opaque string) that maps to server-side KV state. SDKs will surface it to the app rather than replay automatically.
RetryPolicy defaults: exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts=3 for transient-service errors, special handling for rate-limit errors (linear backoff + Retry-After honoring).
Don't surface raw stack traces in human_message for non-dev environments; provide link to troubleshooting doc and include error_id for support lookups.
implementation_plan: 1) Define canonical error taxonomy doc and telemetry schema (this ticket).
2) Implement shared error-code table and stable mappings in runtime core (internal library) used by all SDKs.
3) SDK-specific adaptors: Python exceptions (class + attributes), TS Error subclass with typed fields, Go error type implementing Unwrap/Is with helper functions.
4) Add RetryContext and RetryPolicy helpers to SDK-shared library and publish language-specific APIs.
5) Implement StreamCheckpoint pattern with sample app recipes showing idempotent handlers.
6) End-to-end tests: fault injection harnesses that assert retry decisions and resume flows behave consistently across languages.
7) Docs: migration guide, API reference, telemetry guide, troubleshooting playbook.
examples:
Python: from redwood import RetryPolicy, RetryContext
policy = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, backoff='exponential')
with client.call_retry(policy) as ctx:
    try:
        resp = client.generate(prompt)
    except RedwoodError as e:
        if ctx.should_retry(e):
            # machine_hint present: 'transient'
            # SDK-level helper will not auto-retry side-effecting calls
            raise
        raise

Streaming resume pattern: server sends {data..., checkpoint: 'tkn_xxx'} periodically. Client persists checkpoint. On transient network error client reopens stream and passes checkpoint to server to request missing events. Docs emphasize idempotent handlers and use-cases (progress indicators, logs).
tests_and_validation: Add deterministic unit tests for error->error_class mapping for 30 representative cases (network timeout, connection refused, 429, 503 model OOM, auth 401, malformed request 400).
Build chaos-sim harness that kills connections mid-stream and asserts StreamCheckpoint allows resumption without duplication for idempotent handlers.
Integration smoke for telemetry fields present in traces and logs; sample Kibana dashboard template for SRE.
Cross-language behavioral tests: same fault injection script exercised against Python/TS/Go SDKs to verify consistent retry counts and error_class outputs.
risks: Developers rely on existing brittle string-matching error checks in user code; migration friction for customers.
Automatic resume could introduce duplicated side-effects if users do not follow idempotency guidelines—chosen to be explicit to mitigate this.
Telemetry rollout needs coordination with SRE and log retention policies to ensure error_id is searchable.
Edge cases where model-side degradation returns 200 with degraded payload — SDK must surface model_degraded as an error_class via response metadata to avoid silent quality regressions.
